title: Tenure and resources jointly shape reported household pressure
source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by tenure and monthly income-to-poverty band

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; outcome-specific nonblank universes

observations.method: WPFINWGT with REPWGT1-REPWGT240; Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Design-based standard errors are reported; each outcome has its own nonblank and official conditional universe.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE owned or being bought; THINCPOV below 1.00x.
observations.counterinterpretation: Tenure and resources are correlated with place, family structure, health, debt, and selection into housing; no causal effect is identified.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; outcome-specific nonblank universes

observations.method: Same SIPP/Fay-BRR method and outcome-specific universes as the owner/buyer comparison.
observations.uncertainty: Design-based standard errors are reported; the comparison is descriptive.
observations.counterinterpretation: The renter gap may reflect local prices, household composition, debt, housing quality, or other omitted conditions rather than tenure itself.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; outcome-specific nonblank universes

observations.method: Same SIPP/Fay-BRR method and outcome-specific universes.
observations.uncertainty: Design-based standard errors are reported; this is a high-resource comparison cell, not a security benchmark.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE owned or being bought; THINCPOV 4.00x or more.
observations.counterinterpretation: Ownership can carry mortgage, repair, insurance, and energy exposure not represented by tenure alone.

denominator.unit: positive-final-person-weight selected person-record/month rows; outcome-specific nonblank universes

observations.method: Same SIPP/Fay-BRR method and outcome-specific universes.
observations.uncertainty: Design-based standard errors are reported; the food-hardship contrast is a separate outcome and should not be combined with payment difficulty.
observations.counterinterpretation: High-resource renters may differ from owners in geography, household need, or selection; the table does not establish a causal tenure effect.

related_sources.claim: Official tenure, resource, status-code, and outcome-universe definitions.

boundary: Replicate-weighted descriptive person-record comparison. It does not estimate household prevalence, tenure causation, a dated bill response, health or work displacement, recovery, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.
